── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 27, 37, 53, 40 mi
This week: 42 mi over 5 runs.
Feeling: "Anxious about the new date."
Asks: "The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: You nailed every session of the plan, and with the race pulled to Oct 18 the big miles are already in the bank; next up…
Answers: No, there is not time for a 22, and you do not need one. You already ran 20 miles on Sep 13 and 17 miles last Sunday with a tiny heart-rate drift, which is the fitness signal we wanted.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off to absorb the 17-miler.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145, flat route. Shakes out the long-run legs.
Wed: quality, 10 mi, 2 mi warm up then 5 mi at 8:35/mi marathon pace then 3 mi easy…
Thu: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145. Recovery from the marathon-pace work.
Fri: rest. Second full day off keeps you fresh for the weekend.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, with 4 x 20 sec strides at the end. Primes the legs for Sunday without…
Sun: long, 15 mi, first 11 easy around 9:55/mi then last 4 at 8:35/mi marathon pace…
